descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · S12 Rare or new drug names, where 'or flagged' has to work

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U2 Drug names are transcribed correctly or visibly flagged when uncertain. (UAT TC-23; TFA-94423 AC 4)
  • T7 The dictation vocabulary prompt is ported from the prototype as written, unless Vikram approved a change. (TFA-94229 AC 1; TFA-94229 R1; TFA-94229 R2) — gate: blocked: TFA-94229 in progress

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Same setup as S01/S02; none of these drugs is in DEFAULT_MEDICAL_HINT

When Speak each sentence into the pre-round box

Then Each drug name is spelled correctly, or the uncertain word is visibly flagged in the box

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Correct spelling, or a visible flag on that word (U2). With no flag on main, a misspelling is a Fail (Q2); numbers exact and in order (S01 rule); the result also shows whether the single hint limits recognition (T7, Q9)

Where it ran: local aicheck-dictation (dictation AI checks); test method AICHECK · AI output check; lane planned in the matrix: AI check (automated)

S12 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-23.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Test issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94229 in progress; TFA-94423 ready for qa

Not judged yet: rare or new drug names are blocked on the same OpenAI key approval.

Evidence: allure-results/c6430651…: same key precondition block. Note that main has no drug-name flag UI at all (TC-23 Q2).

Duplicate: the same issue as TC-23/S01; read that one (the kept one). This result carries the label "Duplicate", so a filter can leave it out.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane aicheck-dictation.

Test method: AICHECK · AI output check — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: aicheck-dictation.

Tickets: TFA-94229 Port & preserve Vikram's clinical AI logic (in progress); TFA-94423 Implement GPT-live medical mode for active dictation (ready for qa)

New local lane aicheck-dictation: status blocked in aicheck-dictation/results.json → blocked (blocked).

How it is tested (aicheck-dictation/plan.json, automatable: yes): live, items R-01..R-06 in both contexts; flag UI read from the accessibility tree if one ever exists. — Key precondition only.

Detail:

laneB-preconditions not met: the local OPENAI_API_KEY ends …PUMA and there is no OK on record from Quinn that it is not the key dev uses (her 2026-10-09 notes say it may be), so no audio was sent to OpenAI. Run after that OK: QA_DICT_MODE=live QA_DICTATION_LIVE_OK=PUMA scripts/aicheck-dictation/run.sh. harness self-test with the scripted far end: 2/2 takes landed in the box and passed the checks (shim, Dictate/Stop, read rule, engine attribution, checks.ts). The scripted self-test behind this entry ran before the review fix and used the real prepareSession: each take minted one OpenAI client secret (client.realtime.clientSecrets.create on api.openai.com) with the local key …PUMA — no audio, but the gated key was used.

Evidence: 1 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane B (dictation-ai runner, not built): it plays a fixed synthetic voice into the app's own Dictate through a getUserMedia shim (no real microphone or speaker) on a fresh @roundai.test account, spending the local OpenAI key (laneB-preconditions).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
